text:
maria: Heads-up — started seeing sustained p95 latency spikes for inference egress out of eu-west-1 around 13:04 UTC, also ~0.5% request errors. Looks correlated with a helper batch job that ran at 13:00 and saturated NAT ephemeral ports.
kevin: ugh. can you paste the NAT metrics? sounds like port exhaustion rather than LB or model issue.
maria: logs + grafana snippet: `nat_active_ports -> 65534 -> 95989` (spike), `tcp_conn_states TIME_WAIT high`, and cross-region fail counters rising. attaching screenshot link: https://redwood.internal/g/graph/abcd
josh: hmm we have two failures here to handle: 1) clients pinned to eu-west-1 via latency-based GeoDNS 2) region fallback weights currently set to 0 for eu-central fallback. If eu-west can't egress because of NAT, traffic stays pinned and fails.
ops-oncall: infra-bot fired an alert: `region-egress-error-rate > 0.3%` and health-checks flagged backend pool eu-west-1 as degraded. infra-bot: auto-failover not triggered because health checks still report 200s from a small subset.
kevin: so immediate mitigation: reduce pinning TTL and adjust weights to let latency-based routing move clients to eu-central/na-west. Which DNS config are we using? Route53 weighted+latency?
maria: yes Route53 with latency policy + optional geo override per customer. current TTL is 300s. suggestion: drop to 60 temporarily, enable weighted routing with these weights: eu-west: 20, eu-central: 50, na-west: 30. Also flip fallback policy to prefer same-continent fallback.
josh: we also need sticky session implications for clients doing long-lived sockets to the serving cluster. If we shift DNS, LB session affinity might drop. For websocket/rpc, we should set LB-level fallback to proxy connections to a different region via our global proxy instead of forcing DNS change.
kevin: Agree. Quick plan: 1) add weight changes in Route53 2) push a kube-ingress rule to set `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` and extend idle timeout for RPs 3) add ephemeral NAT port pool on eu-west to give breathing room 4) decrease DNS TTL to 60.
ops-oncall: I'll run the Route53 weight change now (doing weighted change + health check override). tagging @infra-bot to record.
infra-bot: deploy-started route53/traffic-shift v1 by ops-oncall
ops-oncall: route53 update pushed. weights: eu-west=20, eu-central=60, na-west=20. TTL 60. health-check override: enabled for eu-central and na-west.
maria: immediate improvement visible — p95 down by ~30% within 90s. still seeing some TIME_WAIT, but request errors trending back to baseline.
josh: follow-ups: - create a reserve NAT pool for critical pods (10% ports) - add an autoscaling controller for NAT gateways or move to AWS-managed NAT with more capacity - add a GeoDNS fallback policy for region pinning customers that allows cross-continent fallback if error-rate > 0.5% - add runbook step: do not rely solely on health-checks that probe small subset; prefer cross-region synthetic tests across all gateways.
ops-oncall: noted, I'll open infra ticket and schedule the NAT reserve work (priority P2).
kevin: cost note: expect higher inter-region egress while fallback active; ops to alert finance if >$X/day. Maria, can you estimate traffic shift egress?
maria: early estimate: shifting ~12% of EU traffic to na-west adds ~0.08 TB/hour egress to NA, about ~$120/day at current rates if sustained. will refine in ticket.
josh: also add telemetry tag when fallback triggers so Optimize can attribute quality/cost changes to the policy.
infra-bot: deploy-finished route53/traffic-shift v1 success
ops-oncall: thanks everyone. I'll follow-up with ticket links and runbook updates. :thumbsup:
